title: CtlMeResponse
description: Who the server thinks the caller is, and how it decided. This is the ONLY place a client learns its role: the credential carries no role claim, and a subject that verifies but is not on the principal list gets a 403 from this endpoint like from every other (there is no `viewer`-by-default). `auth_method` names the credential that won: `api_key` (X-API-Key ctl key), `bearer` (BV-BRC token), `session` (opaque session id), `local` (`--direct` CLI after the OS identity check — never seen over HTTP, listed so the same schema serves the CLI's `--json` output).

principal.description: Stable principal id: `bvbrc:<user>` for a bearer identity, `key:<label>` for a ctl API key, `local:<uid>` for `--direct`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry of the credential that authenticated this request (token `expiry`, session end); null for a ctl key, which does not expire (it is revoked).

sudo_user.description: `SUDO_USER` observed by the CLI in `--direct` mode, recorded in audit; null over HTTP.
